editorial:
Imagine your teenage daughter starting to spend every waking second on her computer, talking to a boy she met online. That is exactly what happens to Annie, a typical fourteen-year-old living in a nice suburban home. You get to see the story unfold through the eyes of her parents, who start out trusting and supportive but quickly realize something is very wrong. The movie feels like a scary wake-up call because it shows how easy it is for a stranger to trick a kid and a family into believing a total lie. It is a heavy, emotional ride that makes you feel the panic and heartbreak as the secret comes out.

What really makes this work is the acting, especially the parents who look completely broken by the end. The pacing is steady, and while it is not an action movie, the tension keeps you glued to your seat. A downside is that it can be very depressing to watch, but it is an important story for any parent or teen.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a very sad and realistic note. After the truth comes out, the family tries to heal, but the damage is deep. You see that there is no easy fix or happy ending where everything goes back to normal. Annie is left struggling with the trauma of being tricked and abused. The final scenes show a family that is still broken, reminding you that some mistakes change your life forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gripping dramas about family secrets and internet safety.
similarMovies: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
